issue_paraphrase: Setting an explicit numeric offset on the scalar tick formatter does not behave as documented when the value is 1: the setter mistakes it for the boolean True, so instead of forcing the tick labels to be written relative to an offset of 1 it resets the offset to zero and switches on automatic offset selection on the axis. Numeric offset values must be treated as numbers, while only actual booleans should toggle whether offset notation is used at all.
fix_summary: Changed the check in ScalarFormatter.set_useOffset from 'val in [True, False]' to 'isinstance(val, bool)' so that numeric offsets (including 1 and 0) are not confused with boolean switches, and added regression tests for both the boolean and the integer argument forms.

issue_paraphrase: The transform method that reports, separately for the x and y components, whether one transform is contained within another returns wrong answers when the transform is a composite that itself contains a blended (per-axis) transform: both components are reported as not-contained even when the y component actually is contained. Code that relies on this per-axis containment check (for example to decide whether two axes share the same y transform) therefore takes the wrong branch. The answer must also be a pair of booleans, not a list, matching the documented return type.
fix_summary: Added a contains_branch_seperately override to CompositeGenericTransform that delegates to its right-hand (b) transform, and changed the base Transform.contains_branch_seperately to return a tuple instead of a list; the regression assertions were added to the existing test_contains_branch test.
